title.narrative: Multi-sectoral Emergency Response for Cyclone Mocha affected population in Northwest and Rakhine

description.narrative:
ltpgt lt/pgtltp style="margin-bottom:0margin-left:0"gtAlmost 5.4 million people are estimated to have been in the path of Cyclone Mocha. Of these, 3.2 million are considered the most vulnerable, as the massive destruction left by the cyclone adds to the pre-existing poor shelter quality, food insecurity, and poverty levels. Ongoing conflict, displacement, economic crisis and increase in commodities prices had already depleted people’s ability to cater for their needs without resorting to harmful coping strategies. The devastating impact of the cyclone further erodes people’s resilience and deepens their vulnerable situation, exposing them to additional risks. The population affected in Rakhine and Chin States is expected to remain dependent on humanitarian aid until some stability and basic infrastructure – including electricity, water and other basic services – are reestablished. lt/pgtltp style="margin-bottom:0margin-left:0"gt?The project aims to covercritical health and shelter/NFI needs of Cyclone Mocha affected population in Chin and Rakhine. Through this project PIN aims to reach 33,832 cyclone affected population in most affected areas in 1 township (MraukU) in Rakhine and 5 townships (Paletwa, Hakka, Thanglang, Matupi, Kanpalet and Mindat) in Chin, alining with the HRP 2023 strategic objectives for health and shelter/NFI cluster. lt/pgtltp style="margin-bottom:0margin-left:0"gtThrough this funding, PIN will provide medical items to 9 health facilities in Chin State to cover essential medical needs for estimated24000 people.Cash assistance will be provided to 3005 individuals (estimate based on WHO standards -20% of population) in 9 IDP sites in MraukU with chronic health illness with cash assistance for medicines/medical items. lt/pgtltp style="margin-bottom:0margin-left:0"gtShelter Emergency kits and NFI items will be provided to 1,040 fully and partially damaged households in 6 townships in Chin state, Paletwa, Hakka, Thantlang, Matupi, Kanpalet and Mindat. Shelter emergency kits will be provided to 550 HH from IDPs in 9 camp sites in MraukU. lt/pgtltp style="margin-bottom:0margin-left:0"gtPIN will implement the project with 3local partners CHRO and KMSS in Chin and MUCN in Rakhine. PIN's humanitarian response approach for cyclone focuses on strengthening and enabling localized response.lt/pgt
